title: Grasp: Group-based Prediction of Activation Sparsity for Fast LLM Inference
problem: ReLU-fied LLMs (ReLU-based activations enabling sparsity) can skip computation in MLPs with predicted zero activations, but existing sparsity prediction methods suffer from reduced prediction accuracy when dealing with distribution outliers, limiting skipping efficiency and speedup.
motivation: LLM inference is a bottleneck in on-device deployment; MLPs consume significant computation; maximizing sparsity prediction accuracy directly translates to throughput improvements.
method: Grasp is a magnitude-based, training-free sparsity prediction technique building on sign-bit methods for ReLU-fied LLMs. It groups vector elements considering their value distribution within the vector and explicitly handles statistical outliers, allowing more accurate per-element impact estimation. The method efficiently identifies zero activations to enable memory access and computation skipping.
key_novelty: Group-based magnitude prediction with explicit outlier handling for improved activation sparsity prediction in ReLU-fied LLMs.
contributions: Group-based magnitude prediction technique accounting for value distribution within vectors
Explicit outlier detection and handling for accurate sparsity estimation
Training-free sparsity predictor requiring no model modification
11% higher sparsity prediction accuracy than SOTA; 1.85× speedup vs dense inference

metrics.speedup: 1.85× speedup vs dense inference; 11% higher prediction accuracy
metrics.other: higher skipping efficiency enabling memory access skipping

limitations: Limited to ReLU-fied LLMs; applicability to other activation functions (GELU, SiLU) and multi-modal models not discussed.
primary_theme: group-based sparsity prediction for accelerating ReLU-fied LLM inference
